response:
I don't have file or repo access in this session, so this is feedback on the document as written — I haven't verified any of the `file:line` claims.

## The big one: this is a status register wearing a plan's clothes

Two different documents are fighting inside it. There's a findings/decision register (what was audited, what was decided, what's on whose desk) and there's executable work (P0's nine items, the rename PR, the Inspect swap). The register parts are good. The executable parts aren't executable by anyone without your context: no goal statement, no ordering, no file-level task decomposition, no test or commit points, no acceptance criteria. P0 is the only section that names files and lines — and per your own header it's already shipped.

Split it. Keep this as the register. Write a separate plan for the work that's actually queued (rename execution, #310 round 2, the reference-file edits from #302(i), the G>=8 batch, the ADOPT swap), with tasks that a fresh engineer could pick up cold.

## The document contradicts itself

The header was updated on 29-Jul; the body wasn't.

- Header: "ADR 0097 skill-assay rename... owner CONFIRMED 29-Jul." P2b: "Decide: rename plugin vs README disambiguation... suffices." That call is closed but still reads as open.
- Header: "P1 DECIDED (ADR 0095)." P1 still presents options (a)/(b)/(c) with no record of which won. Anyone reading P1 alone will re-litigate it. Replace the options with the chosen option plus the residual work — right now the only trace of that residual is the header's "first G>=8 batch."
- Header: "P0 SHIPPED (#320)." All nine P0 items still read as pending.
- P2b: "fixed in PR #321" sits inside a section whose framing is "owner call."

The status paragraph itself is a run-on encoding roughly ten states across two PRs and six ADRs. A table would do it better: item | ADR | PR | decided? | implemented? | merged? | owner.

## The priority ordering reproduces the failure it diagnoses

The verdict paragraph is the best writing here — 100% of open work went to the measuring apparatus, and grok's "cleanup of the lab's conscience" line is quoted against interest. Then the plan puts P0, P1, P2, P2b, and a ~10pd substrate swap ahead of the one section addressing lever 1, and gates P3 behind P1 on top of that. P3 gets three lines, no owner, no date, no deliverable.

A stop-list with no start date isn't a stop-list. If lever 1 is the goal's first lever, give it a capacity floor that bites — e.g. no further instrument PR merges until building-skills iteration 4 is in review — or promote it. Related gap: "adopter-felt skill quality" is named as the lever but never operationalized, so P3 has no definition of done. A measured MERGE on iter4? Adopter feedback? Say which.

## The 10pd Inspect swap gets one clause

It's the largest line item in the document and it lives inside a parenthetical in the status header. Missing: scope, what the adapter seam actually covers, what breaks (`benchstats.py`? `clustered_delta`? existing benchmark dirs?), rollback, test plan.

The first-order question isn't in there at all: **are pre-swap and post-swap results poolable?** If Inspect doesn't reproduce the paired-delta/clustered analysis, the swap doesn't cost 10pd — it costs 10pd plus the comparability of every existing benchmark, in a repo already carrying re-measure debt. Answer that before approving the spend.

## Statistics — mostly sound, three soft spots

**Good:** the coverage sim is well-designed (3 DGPs, paired design matched to the live estimator) and "residual is POWER, not interval family" is the right read. Keep t.

1. "Strong claims need G>=8" is a number without a justification. You give MDE ~0.35 at G=6 but never state the minimum interesting effect or target power, so G>=8 is unfalsifiable as a bar — and P1's batched re-measure inherits the vagueness. Publish MDE at G=8 and G=10, the effect you care about, and the power you're buying.
2. #302's kill rests on "the plausible effect collapses below the G=10 MDE." That's an argument you can't detect it, not that it isn't there — worth stating plainly, because the same logic would kill nearly any small-effect measurement. It also boomerangs on C5: if guide-level omissions are undetectable at G=10, why would building-skills-vs-bare be detectable? Either C5 is powered and you show why, or it's dead on arrival.
3. #317's "n-grams UNDERSTATE the real coupling" is a single-source, non-blinded qualitative read being used to override a measured number. It may well be right, but label it hypothesis-grade — the task-value-outcomes requirement is being adopted on that basis.

## Unstated dependency that matters most

You correctly refuse to measure /sweep through a contested DV. But P1's batched re-measure and P3's two re-measures are *also* doctrine-heavy skills running through that same DV, and the plan never says whether they inherit #317's task-value requirement. That ordering — #317 DV decision → re-measure bar → P1 batch and P3 — is the critical path and it's invisible. Add an explicit dependency list; it'll also surface that P1 blocks #252, P3, and the re-measure bar while simultaneously being listed as decided.

## Owner actions aren't extractable

"/decide each," "owner call," "owner direction," "awaiting owner merge" — scattered across four sections. Add a five-line "on the owner's desk now" block at the top: merge #321; decide #310 disposition; decide #317 DV; approve/deny the 10pd Inspect spend; confirm the P3 capacity floor.

## Smaller things

- **#303 evidence is a scratchpad.** `scratchpad coverage303.py` + "results table in session log" won't be reproducible in three months. Land the sim in the repo before closing, or the close is unauditable.
- **P0.8** — "measure headroom first" is an unspecified step. Say what the budget is and where it's checked.
- **P0.9** bundles three unrelated fixes and says "stated in 4 files" without naming them. That's a count the executor has to re-derive; name the paths.
- **Dates** are inconsistent (`28-Jul`, `22-Jun-2026`, `13-Jul`) and mostly year-less. This doc will be read next year.
- **"P2b"** as a label signals a late insert. If it gates a rename PR that "executes LAST," it isn't a P2 appendix.

## Keep

The verdict paragraph naming the failure mode; soliciting and quoting a third-party opinion against interest; killing the $25 grid after a zero-cost read; refusing a cheap KEEP on /sweep through a contested DV. That's unusually honest bench discipline — the problems above are organizational, not epistemic.
